paragraphs: Thunder rolled in off the bay, except the bay was a bathtub, and the town on its shore was built from cereal boxes, which made Yellow Duck Sweater exactly the right size to be worried. Hail bounced off the cardboard roofs like dropped rice. Then the bathwater bulged, and up rose Godzilla: gray-green and pebbly, with spines like a row of chipped plates and eyes as big as the duck's whole head. It took one step onto the shore. It wobbled. It took another and sat down hard on the post office.

The duck knew that sit. It was the sit of an early checkpoint, when the legs had opinions and the floor came up fast. So the duck walked out where the monster could see it, slowly: lean, step, catch, step. The monster leaned. The monster stepped. Its tail knocked a water tower into the tub with a plop, but it stayed up. Down Main Street they went, one small teacher and one enormous student, the duck quacking a reward point for every good step. At the end of the street the monster lay down with its chin on the beach, and the duck sat in the warm hollow between two of its spines, out of the hail, listening to a heartbeat as slow as a washing machine.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The robot duck stands on the main street of a small town made of cereal boxes beside a big bathtub full of water, while hailstones bounce off the cardboard roofs on a stormy night. Panel 2: The bathwater bulges and a huge friendly gray-green lizard monster with pebbly skin and jagged plate-like spines rises out of the tub, towering over the tiny robot duck. Panel 3: The giant lizard monster wobbles onto the shore and sits down hard on a little cardboard post office, while the robot duck watches from the street with its head tilted. Panel 4: The robot duck walks slowly down the street leaning forward, and the giant lizard monster carefully copies its step right behind it. Panel 5: The giant lizard monster's tail knocks a little cardboard water tower into the bathtub with a splash as it walks behind the robot duck, which quacks up at it encouragingly. Panel 6: The giant lizard monster lies on the bathtub beach with its chin resting on the sand, and the robot duck sits snugly in the hollow between two of its spines, sheltered from the falling hail. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
